script: Entitled "woman" has a hissy fit over legos. I was at a garage sale, scrolling through a pile of random junk, when I spotted a tiny tub of Legos and thought, "Why not?" I asked the lady running the sale if I could set my stuff on a table, and she said, "Sure, just put it on the little table." So I did, making a pile of my own stuff next to the Legos. But here's the thing… I left the table to check out some clothes, and five minutes later I see the same lady lugging the exact tub I'd left. I said, "Hey, sorry, I am male actually, I am going to get those." She replied, "Well, I've been holding them for ten minutes." What I didn't know was that I'd already piled them off the table 25-30 minutes ago. I told her, "They were in my pile." She said, "They were just on a table." And that's when everything changed. I pointed to the table where the rest of my stuff was and she said, "Oh yeah, sorry, those are his." The stakes were high: if she didn't get them back, I'd lose the Legos and maybe the $5 I'd pay. I didn't want to lose my weekend or my budget. I had to get them back, or I'd be stuck with nothing. I asked the organizer about the price, and she said, "$5." She had no idea the Legos came from my pile. I said, "Those are from my pile." She asked, "Which pile is yours?" I pointed, and she sighed, "Oh yeah, sorry." Little did I know this was just the beginning of the drama. The lady whispered, "This is unfair, I was carrying those for ten minutes." I didn't think much of it at first. However… a few minutes later the organizer told me the lady was back at the counter five times, throwing a fit about the Legos. I said, "Fine, just give them to her. I don't want you to deal with her, and there's just Legos." They handed the tub over, the lady stopped her hissy fit, checked out, and left. If this didn't work, I'd lose everything I had spent on the day, and that's a big deal. I was relieved the conflict ended, but I wondered, "Am I in the wrong?" I wasn't, honestly. The lady had a point about ownership, but I had already set my claim. In the end, it was a small lesson in respecting boundaries at a garage sale. And that's how I learned that even a tub of Legos can stir up a whole drama.
